title.value: Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer
title.justification: The title captures the essence of the paper's content, focusing on a recipe for creating a scalable graph transformer.
title.quote: Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer

extractions.description: The paper proposes a framework for constructing scalable graph transformers, called GPS, which supports various types of positional and structural encodings. It aims to optimize graph representation learning by combining local message-passing mechanisms with global attention mechanisms. The architecture addresses the limitations of previous graph transformers, making it suitable for large graphs with linear complexity. GPS demonstrates competitive results across multiple benchmarks without explicit edge features in the attention module, potentially benefiting real-world applications like chemical interaction modeling and robotic control.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper does not explicitly focus on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development but rather on enhancing the computational efficiency and scalability of graph transformers.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Graph Transformers (GTs) alleviate fundamental limitations pertaining to the sparse message passing mechanism, e.g., over-smoothing, over-squashing, and expressiveness bounds, by allowing nodes to attend to all other nodes in a graph (global attention).

primary_category.justification: The central theme of the paper is related to computational advancements in graph learning techniques rather than direct applications to climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: We propose a recipe on how to build a general, powerful, scalable (GPS) graph Transformer with linear complexity and state-of-the-art results on a diverse set of benchmarks.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper's contents are not directly relevant to any secondary areas of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_categories.quote: We provide a modular framework G RAPH GPS that supports multiple types of encodings and that provides efficiency and scalability both in small and large graphs.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no specific sub-category under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development that this paper aligns with, as its focus is on graph transformer architecture.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our GPS recipe consists of choosing 3 main ingredients: (i) positional/structural encoding, (ii) local message-passing mechanism, and (iii) global attention mechanism.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories are relevant as the paper is technical and focuses on graph transformer models, not sustainability subjects.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The increased expressivity thus provides double benefit to our hybrid MPNN+Transformer architecture.

applications.value: real-world applications like modeling chemical interactions and robotic control
applications.justification: These applications are mentioned as potential areas where the discussed graph transformer models might be beneficial, although not directly related to sustainable development.
applications.quote: This benefits several real-world applications, such as modeling chemical interactions beyond the covalent bonds, or graph-based robotic control.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on deep learning advancements rather than introducing a new sustainable development category.
new_primary_category.quote: We propose a recipe on how to build a general, powerful, scalable (GPS) graph Transformer with linear complexity and state-of-the-art results on a diverse set of benchmarks.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category is needed as the paper is focused on algorithmic improvements in deep learning, and not directly on sustainability matters.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Global attention incurs quadratic computational costs O(N 2) for a graph with N nodes and E edges, that limits GTs to small graphs with up to a few hundred nodes.
